lead_headline: Restaurant inventory hits 75 leads (36 openings, 39 closures) as March closes with 2 fresh additions—foreclosure filings slide to softest weekly count since mid-February, subscriptions post +1 net Monday bounce

restaurant.blurb: 2 new leads today (1 opening, 1 closure) hold active inventory at 75—matching weekend peak but shedding weekend's velocity. Monday adds: Denver Café & Kava non-alcoholic kava bar soft-opens 5501 E Colfax (Colfax corridor expansion, February media surge); Dairy Queen Grill & Chill flags 7960 Sheridan Westminster closure, replaced by Blazing Bird Nashville hot chicken concept. March's 75-case close surges 37% above February's 55-lead exit—Q1's strongest monthly tally driven by downtown corridor density (Union Station logs 8 opening leads alone) and closure acceleration in suburban Dairy Queen/franchise consolidations. Lead quality climbs: 89% carry confidence scores 8+, flagging Claude verification rigor vs raw scraping noise. Week's standout thread: three separate Dairy Queen closures (Westminster, Littleton×2) signal metro franchise retrenchment as fast-casual competition intensifies.

foreclosure.blurb: 34 filings this week drop 19% from prior week's 42—March's softest period outside holiday windows—with top case at $686K Arapahoe property (24296 E Ohio Drive) as zero $2M+ outliers mark first sub-million ceiling since mid-February; 74 auctions scheduled next 7 days.

liquor.blurb: Zero applications today extend March's statewide drought to 31 consecutive days—tomorrow's April 1 quarterly deadline now critical inflection point. Sustained silence past Tuesday would confirm systemic database lag vs organic demand collapse across metro hospitality sector. Archive context: 12,316 tracked cases show no comparable void—previous longest stretch capped at 12 days during 2024 winter holiday window. If database resumes April 1, expect backlog surge of 40-60 applications representing suppressed March activity; if silence persists, escalate to state Liquor Enforcement Division for system status confirmation.

reputation.blurb: 62 mentions this week climb 19% from prior period's 52—fifth consecutive weekly gain as Instagram claims 32% share (20 citations), outpacing Denver Post's 9 pickups. Monday's 3 mentions include Denver Post space coverage, Threads Denver Gazette cross-post, and Rocky Mountain Voice x.com pickup. Week's diversification accelerates: social platforms (Instagram, x.com, Facebook, Threads) now command 52% total vs legacy media's 21%—inverting historical 60%/40% split. Top story threads: Denver Water 20% reduction mandate drives Instagram cascade; Broncos stadium progress fuels multi-platform pickup; Centennial office listing cycles through Post real estate desk. Four-week rolling average settles at 55 mentions/week (+16% vs Q1 baseline), projecting 2,860 annual citations if April sustains March's momentum.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +1 yesterday (1 new, 0 canceled) lifts MTD to +55 (+1.8/day), 90-day net to +126. Monday's solo acquisition breaks weekend flatline—prior Saturday-Sunday delivered zero net movement, matching March 21-22 stall pattern. Recent divergence sharpens: past 7 days post +16 net (28 new, 12 canceled, 2.3/day) vs prior week's +20 (30 new, 10 canceled, 2.9/day)—acquisition volume dips 7% while churn climbs 20%, signaling retention pressure building into Q2. Longer arc: 90-day +126 tracks 39% ahead of YTD's +1.4/day baseline, but March 23-30 churn acceleration (1.7 canceled/day vs 1.0 historical average) flags vulnerability. March needs +3 net today (final day) to hit +58 monthly close, matching February's +1.9/day pace—achievable if Monday's zero-churn pattern holds through Tuesday.
